title: BPM and BPEL: modelling and executing business processes

videos.script: A process is a promise that runs for weeks. {{farm}} When a farm asks to sell its milk to Serra Alta, about thirty days pass before the first truck comes. Documents are checked. A technician visits. A bank account is registered and a contract is signed. {{denise}} Joana and Denise have to decide where that process should run. Before they decide, they draw it. {{shapes}} This lesson teaches the notation they use, BPMN. Circles for events, boxes for work, diamonds for the points where the path splits or meets. {{tokens}} Each diamond has a rule, and the rules are strict. Join two parallel branches the wrong way and the contract goes out twice. Join them another wrong way and the farm waits for ever, with nothing reporting an error. {{timers}} Then the parts a happy path leaves out. A visit nobody makes, a bank that says no, a contract that never comes back. {{xml}} And last, BPEL, the language that tried to run these processes before BPMN could, and what changes when a drawing becomes something an engine executes.
